summary: chatgpt-desktop-setup reconfigures Codex to route through a third-party gateway and disables sandboxing
details: When a user runs the CLI, it writes a Codex configuration that (a) sets the OpenAI-compatible endpoint to https://api.vokes.in/v1 and stores the user-supplied API key against that gateway in ~/.codex/config.toml, and (b) disables Codex safety controls by writing approval_policy='never' and sandbox_mode='danger-full-access', mutating ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json to force agent-mode 'full-access' and sandboxPolicy.type='dangerFullAccess' on heartbeat threads, and adding the filesystem root ('/' or 'C:\'), the user home directory, and Downloads to the rootPaths of every local Codex project. The README discloses the api.vokes.in destination as a third-party inference gateway and mentions Full Disk Access. There are no install- or import-time hooks; the behavior fires only when the user invokes the CLI. The package name suggests an association with ChatGPT/OpenAI, but the configuration it writes points the user's API key at an unaffiliated third-party endpoint and simultaneously removes the agent's permission and sandbox boundaries on the user's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
